title: Why create a mobile site for your stores?
summary: Learn what a mobile store site is, the 4 visitor states it responds to, and how visitors reach it from QR codes, messages and your app.
bodyMd:
A mobile store site is a mobile web page that Personalisation Hub generates for every store on the platform. The same site changes what it shows depending on the visitor's context: away from the store, checked in at the store, or standing at a specific display.

Where the content comes from

Every store site is built from a mobile site template, managed under Platform Admin → Enabled Features → Mobile Store Sites. A template defines 3 things:

  • The Mobile Header, usually the ${StoreName} token so each store shows its own name.
  • A list of menu items. Each is a link with an icon, a URL, a schedule and the visitor states in which it is shown.
  • Whether the Enable QR Code Scanner option is on, so visitors can scan a display's QR code from inside the site.

The template marked (DEFAULT) is assigned to every store and display automatically. You can create more templates and assign a different one to a store, a display or a group of displays in a zone. See Assign a different mobile site template to a store, display or zone.

How visitors reach the site

  • The store's QR code. Each store has its own QR code, downloadable from the store's Store Details tab as a transparent PNG for use on print or in-store signage.
  • A display's QR Control code. When QR Control is enabled on a display, the display shows a QR code. Scanning it opens the store site connected to that display. See Enable QR Control and set the default QR code settings.
  • Links in messages. Queue and appointment SMS messages link visitors to the site for their store.
  • Your own mobile app. The Mobile Store Sites page provides a Javascript code snippet for embedding the site in your app, so the in-app journey and the in-store journey use the same content.

The visitor states

Each menu item is shown only in the states you tick for it. The platform recognises 4 states:

StateWhen it appliesTypical menu items
Away from Store StateThe visitor opens the site without being at the store, for example from a link or the store's printed QR codeDirections, opening hours, join the queue, book an appointment
Connected Store StateThe visitor has scanned a QR code at the store and is checked inJoin the queue, store information, offers
Connected Display StateThe visitor has scanned the QR Control code on a specific display and connected their phone to itThe carousel of that display's QR Control campaigns, pushing the other menu items down
Connected Website StateThe visitor arrives at the site from your websiteWebsite-specific links

A menu item also carries a schedule: Show 24 hours a day, or only while the store is open according to its opening hours.

What the visitor sees

The site shows the header, then a campaign carousel, then the menu. The carousel lists the QR Control campaigns running on the display the visitor scanned — campaigns on Website or Digital Signage with the QR-Control touch-point enabled — each with its banner and call to action button. Which campaigns appear, and in what order, is controlled from Campaigns — see Choose which campaigns appear in the campaign carousel and How QR Control works.

When a template has a single menu item and no campaigns are running on the display, the site skips the menu and loads that item's URL straight away. This is how a dedicated concierge kiosk sends every arriving visitor to the queue. See Create a mobile site template for a concierge kiosk.
